mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is accompanied by a simultaneous strong rise in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when INDPRO is rising concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclicals and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed when FEDFUNDS is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a simultaneous monetary tightening and inflation acceleration, increasing real discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a supply shock (INDPRO falls sharply).

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-on-month increase in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) combined with a simultaneous rise in consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) signals robust household demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise month-on-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a sharp rise in unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as monetary tightening follows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when CPIAUCSL is not rising concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction-related earnings and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed when FEDFUNDS is simultaneously cut.
